subject: sentences
title: Pick the end mark
about: He reads a sentence with its end mark missing and taps the period, question mark or exclamation point. North Carolina wants first graders to recognize, name and use all three.
tip: Have him read the sentence with his voice going up for a question or big for an exclamation, then pick the mark.

cards.q: Which end mark? The cat is on the mat
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? The cat is on the mat.
cards.note: A telling sentence is a statement. It ends with a period.

cards.q: Which end mark? I have two red socks
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? I have two red socks.
cards.note: This sentence tells about socks. A statement ends with a period.

cards.q: Which end mark? My dog can dig
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? My dog can dig.
cards.note: This sentence tells what a dog can do. A statement ends with a period.

cards.q: Which end mark? We went to the shop
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? We went to the shop.
cards.note: This sentence tells where we went. A statement ends with a period.

cards.q: Which end mark? The sun is hot
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? The sun is hot.
cards.note: This sentence tells a fact in a calm voice. A statement ends with a period.

cards.q: Which end mark? Where is my hat
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Where is my hat?
cards.note: An asking sentence is a question. It ends with a question mark.

cards.q: Which end mark? Can you jump
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Can you jump?
cards.note: This sentence asks something. A question ends with a question mark.

cards.q: Which end mark? What is in the box
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? What is in the box?
cards.note: It starts with the asking word what. A question ends with a question mark.

cards.q: Which end mark? Who has the cup
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Who has the cup?
cards.note: It starts with the asking word who. A question ends with a question mark.

cards.q: Which end mark? Do you like jam
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Do you like jam?
cards.note: Your voice goes up at the end when you ask. A question ends with a question mark.

cards.q: Which end mark? Wow, what a big fish
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Wow, what a big fish!
cards.note: A sentence with strong feeling is an exclamation. It ends with an exclamation point.

cards.q: Which end mark? Ouch, that is hot
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Ouch, that is hot!
cards.note: Ouch shows a big feeling. An exclamation ends with an exclamation point.

cards.q: Which end mark? Look out, a bug
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Look out, a bug!
cards.note: Look out is said in a big voice. An exclamation ends with an exclamation point.

cards.q: Which end mark? Hooray, we won
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Hooray, we won!
cards.note: Hooray shows a happy feeling. An exclamation ends with an exclamation point.

cards.q: Which end mark? Help, I am stuck
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Help, I am stuck!
cards.note: Help is called out in a big voice. An exclamation ends with an exclamation point.
